research_question: Does the inference from God's having no proper parts to God's being part of all of God's parts require bivalence or determinacy for the relevant parthood relation?

premises.text: Divine simplicity is most plausibly understood as the claim that God lacks proper parts.
premises.quote: Instead, DDS is more plausibly understood as saying that God lacks proper parts – call this the mereological formulation of DDS.

premises.text: If proper parthood is non-symmetric parthood, the claim that God has no proper parts yields the symmetry formulation of divine simplicity.
premises.quote: But if proper parthood is defined as non-symmetric parthood, then explicating proper parthood in the mereological formulation yields the symmetry formulation of DDS.

premises.text: Instantiation can be modelled as parthood because objects may be understood as mereological fusions of their properties.
premises.quote: On the mereological bundle theory suggested by Laurie Paul (2002, 2006, 2012, 2017), for instance, objects are mereological fusions of the properties they bear.

premises.text: God and omniscience can be mutual parts with respect to similarity while remaining numerically distinct.
premises.quote: it is also possible, at least in principle, for this symmetric parthood relation to hold while God remains numerically distinct from his omniscience.

premises.text: Defining proper parthood as non-symmetric similarity-based parthood makes proper parthood irreflexive, asymmetric, and transitive.
premises.quote: If proper parthood is defined as non-symmetric parthood with respect to similarity, it would immediately be irreflexive, asymmetric, and transitive.

missing_premise.text: Proper parthood is non-symmetric parthood, and the symmetry formulation of divine simplicity is the thesis that God is part of all God's parts.

conclusion.text: Divine simplicity can viably be formulated as the thesis that God is part of all God’s parts.

challenged_premise.text: If proper parthood is non-symmetric parthood, the claim that God has no proper parts yields the symmetry formulation of divine simplicity.

objection: A theologian maintains a three-valued parthood catalogue. It records omniscience as part of God, while whether God is part of omniscience is explicitly undetermined. A proper part is defined as a part whose reverse parthood is false, not merely unconfirmed. Omniscience is therefore not a proper part of God, and the catalogue contains no other candidate parts, so “God has no proper parts” is true. Yet “God is part of all God’s parts” is not true, because God’s parthood of omniscience remains undetermined. The absence of asymmetric parthood does not establish reciprocal parthood when undetermined relations are permitted. Premise W7212186029.c008 fails because having no proper parts does not yield symmetry when reverse parthood can be neither true nor false.

strongest_responses.response: The objection is valid under the proposed three-valued catalogue: a part of God can have an undetermined reverse parthood relation without counting as a proper part under the stated definition. The inference works only if reverse parthood for every part of God is settled true rather than merely not false.
strongest_responses.why_it_failed: Defender A could not derive this determinacy condition from the existing claims. The reply therefore concedes that c008 fails as stated and requires an added bivalence premise.

strongest_responses.response: The intended account treats a part as proper when reverse parthood fails, and, given bivalence, the absence of proper parts entails reciprocal parthood. The similarity-relative relation is said to have determinate structural features, so the three-valued catalogue challenges only an unrestricted reading.
strongest_responses.why_it_failed: The response reaches the desired conclusion only by explicitly adding determinacy or bivalence. Calling this a small semantic repair does not show that the condition was already present in c008 or established by the surrounding argument.

open_questions: Can the required bivalence or determinacy condition be justified from the metaphysics of similarity-relative parthood, rather than stipulated for the inference?
Does the account's claim that proper parthood is irreflexive, asymmetric, and transitive rule out truth-value gaps, and if so, under which logic?
Should 'non-symmetric parthood' mean reverse parthood is false, not true, or determinate in some stronger sense?
Would adding bivalence preserve the proposed distinction between mutual similarity-relative parthood and numerical identity?
paper_direction: A paper here would argue that the symmetry formulation of divine simplicity is not entailed by the absence of proper parts unless the underlying parthood relation is bivalent or otherwise determinate. Its central case would be the three-valued countermodel, in which omniscience is part of God while the reverse relation is undetermined, so omniscience is not a proper part but reciprocal parthood does not follow. The strongest reply to anticipate is that the intended similarity-relative parthood relation already carries determinate structural features and that bivalence is only a clarification. The paper would need to show either that those features do not entail determinacy, making the repair substantively additional, or that an independently motivated semantics supplies determinacy and thereby restores the inference.

reasons.coherence: The objection is internally consistent and targets the right step, but it reaches c008 only by changing the logic and choosing one of several definitions of 'proper part,' not by engaging the premise as the source states it.
reasons.robustness: The obvious reply is that the argument is classical and the gap is unmotivated. Neither the transcript nor the direction answers this beyond noting that bivalence is an extra premise, which the defender treats as a trivial, already implicit assumption.
reasons.significance: If it succeeded, the paper would mostly record that a classical equivalence needs classical logic. That is a small refinement unless it is tied to a substantive case for vague or indeterminate similarity-based parthood, which the direction only gestures at in its open questions.
reasons.specificity: There is a definite thesis and a central countermodel, but the plan does not say which three-valued logic is used, does not engage the definitional alternatives, and does not give a positive motivation for gaps, so the work it would actually do remains underdetermined.

assessment.strongest_objection: The point is a generic feature of nonclassical logic, not a discovery about divine simplicity: c008 is stated in classical mereology, where 'no x with Pxg and not-Pgx' is equivalent to 'every part of God has God as a part.' Any classical equivalence can be broken by adding truth-value gaps. The countermodel also depends on a chosen definition of 'proper part' (reverse parthood false rather than not true). On the alternative definition, or under strong Kleene evaluation, 'God has no proper parts' comes out undetermined rather than true, and the alleged counterexample disappears. Without an independent reason to think divine parthood is gappy, the paper refutes a reading nobody holds.
assessment.what_it_needs: It must give an independent, non-stipulative reason why similarity-relative parthood admits indeterminacy, for example that similarity comes in degrees and so yields vague parthood. It must also show that under every reasonable definition of 'proper part' in that setting, the step from 'no proper parts' to symmetry fails.
assessment.summary: As framed, this is a logic-textbook observation dressed up as an objection to divine simplicity; it becomes a paper only if the author can show that similarity-relative parthood is independently liable to indeterminacy.

revision.research_question: Does the inference from God having no proper parts to God being part of all of God's parts require bivalence or determinacy for the similarity-relative parthood relation, and under which definitions of 'proper part' does that dependence arise?
revision.paper_direction: A paper here would argue that the step from 'God has no proper parts' to the symmetry formulation of divine simplicity (God is part of all God's parts) holds under classical semantics, and fails only if the parthood relation admits truth-value gaps together with one specific definition of proper part, namely 'reverse parthood is false' rather than 'reverse parthood is not true'. The paper would proceed in three steps. First, it would show that under the 'not true' definition, and under strong Kleene evaluation, the three-valued countermodel does not falsify the conditional, because the antecedent is then false or undetermined, so the counterexample depends on a single definitional choice. Second, it would give an independent motivation for gaps: similarity comes in degrees, and similarity-relative parthood inherits that gradation, so some pairs such as 'God is part of omniscience' may lack a determinate value. This is a substantive claim the paper must argue, not assume. Third, it would state the result as a conditional: the symmetry formulation follows from the absence of proper parts whenever reverse parthood is bivalent for the relevant pairs. The central thesis is therefore a bounded claim about the dependence of the inference on bivalence, not a refutation of divine simplicity or of the classical argument.
revision.reply_to_strongest_objection: The paper concedes the referee's central point: in classical mereology c008 holds, and the three-valued countermodel works only with the reverse-false definition of proper part. Under the not-true definition, omniscience counts as a proper part, so 'no proper parts' is false and the conditional is not falsified. Under strong Kleene evaluation, 'no proper parts' is undetermined, so again no counterexample arises. The paper therefore does not claim that c008 is refuted in general. It claims that the inference depends on bivalence under one definitional choice, and it supplies the motivating case for gaps by appeal to degreed similarity yielding vague parthood, argued in the paper rather than assumed. If that motivation fails, the result reduces to a remark about classical equivalence, and the paper states this openly.
revision.what_changed: The thesis is narrowed from a general refutation of premise c008 to a conditional claim that the inference depends on bivalence under the reverse-false definition, with an explicit argument for gaps and an open concession that the result is small if that argument fails.

reasons.coherence: The objection is internally consistent and does target c008. However, it bears on a non-classical reading the original argument never adopts, so it is aimed at a different claim rather than the premise as stated.
reasons.robustness: The direction itself concedes that if the gap motivation fails, nothing but a classical-equivalence remark remains. Its gap motivation (degreed similarity) is gestured at, not developed, and invites the obvious reply that degrees are not gaps and that divine indeterminacy is independently implausible.
reasons.significance: Even if successful, it adds only a bivalence proviso to a step every reader already understands as classical, which is at most a minor footnote to the symmetry formulation debate.
reasons.specificity: It has a definite bounded thesis, a concrete three-step plan, and an explicit statement of what must be argued (the gap motivation), though the key second step is underspecified.

assessment.strongest_objection: The result is a textbook logical fact rather than a finding about divine simplicity. In any gappy logic, ¬∃x(Pxg ∧ ¬Pgx) fails to entail ∀x(Pxg → Pgx) without excluded middle. c008 is stated within a classical mereology where proper parthood is defined by non-symmetry, so the countermodel changes the logic instead of finding a flaw. Worse, the proposed motivation for gaps, degreed similarity, sits poorly with simplicity theorists. They will deny that God's nature admits indeterminacy, and degreed similarity more naturally yields degrees of parthood than gaps.
assessment.what_it_needs: It must show that the similarity-relative parthood relation in the target account is independently committed to indeterminacy, and that a simplicity theorist cannot deny this without cost. That means engaging the vague-composition and indeterminate-identity literature (Evans-style arguments, Sider, Barnes and Williams on metaphysical indeterminacy) and showing the dependence is a real liability. Otherwise the paper only records that a classical equivalence fails in Kleene logic.
assessment.summary: A clearly organised but thin proposal: its core result is a standard fact about three-valued logic, and it becomes a paper only if the author can show the target account is genuinely committed to indeterminate divine parthood.
